data.body:
CLOSED. Change 1146 is LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 (patchset 2, 749bc2b41). Closing UNBLOCKED 172e.

FULL LOCAL SUITE on the final tree: 8273 passed, 74 skipped, 1 failed, 2 errors in 28m49s. ALL
THREE NON-PASSES DIAGNOSED AS ARTIFACTS, NOT REGRESSIONS, and each RE-RUN GREEN on the clean tree
(3 passed) rather than argued away:

  2 ERRORS -- both the suite's own HEAD-movement guard (tests/conftest.py:448) reporting
    "Test moved the repo HEAD (b4b475b042 -> ead36bdb2b)" and "(ead36bdb2b -> 749bc2b416)". Those
    two transitions are MY commit and MY amend, made while the suite was running. The guard cannot
    tell an agent's concurrent commit from a test's stray commit, so it blamed the tests.
    IMPORTANT: the guard's remedy text says to undo the stray commits with `git reset --hard
    ead36bdb2b`. DO NOT run it -- those are real commits, and following that advice would have
    destroyed the amend that fixed the CI drift. Do not run the full suite concurrently with
    commits in the same worktree.
  1 FAILURE -- test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys, "gen_env_registry.py --check stale".
    A TRUE positive for the tree at suite START: the run was launched before docs/env-vars.md was
    regenerated. Same root cause as the patchset-1 Verified -1, already fixed. It is the local
    twin of that CI gate, so the suite would have caught it had it finished first.

ACs verified by running their literal commands, not by inspection:
  grep -n "claude-" src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml -> no output, exit 1 (no
    "claude-" anywhere in the file); the ladder block now reads trivial / standard / frontier.
  the config.py module-level model_classes import guard one-liner -> prints False.
All 16 contract tests green; 10 of them were held out from the implementer and passed unseen.

NOTE FOR THE NEXT TICKET, this cost nothing here but will recur: implementing a plan STALES ITS OWN
scoped attestation. At close time 7761 read stale-code naming exactly the 5 files in its own
file_impact (code_review/batch_runner.py, config.py, production_batch_runner.py, sizing.py,
plan-review.yaml) -- i.e. the drift WAS the delivery. The close gate accepted it anyway and exited
0, so stale-CODE at close is tolerated. That is different from stale-MATERIAL (an edited plan),
which the 7f86 trail records as forcing a full fresh plan review. Do not "fix" a stale-code reading
at close time by re-running the review; it is the expected end state of doing the work.
